title: Refuse readings that drop or defer a part the request names
summary: Retry of job 20261029-111202-2bpc, which stopped in planning round 3. Add check_request_coverage, called from check_reading_acceptance in reading.rs, so a reading that drops or defers a numbered part or Acceptance bullet of the request is refused. This time the parser covers (N), N), N. and lettered forms, and the matching rules are specified and checked before code. The audience is the reader/verifier pipeline.

defaults_applied.how: Fixed in check_reading_acceptance, the gate every reading passes.
New tests plus fmt, clippy and cargo test criteria.
Criteria run the real gate on readings that defer parts.
The rule is enforced in code, with a READING_RULES line for the reader.
Doc comment and CHANGELOG name the cause and cite jobs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (is_bullet at 1992, request_text_acceptance at 2002, check_reading_acceptance at 2599, check_governance_coverage at 2674, scoped_reading test helper at 4992) and crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (READING_RULES at 1557, the rule-section test asserting under 2400 bytes at about 3193). The new check runs after check_governance_coverage inside check_reading_acceptance, so first attempts and retries both pass it. No record or data file is added, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected. The property is measured by calling the real gate, not a stand-in.

Job 20261029-111202-2bpc is addressed finding by finding. (1) Major, parser dropped N) and N.: parse (N), N), N. and lettered (a)/a) runs. Runs must start at 1 (or a), have at least two markers, and each part needs a distinctive word. (2) Major, stem rules refused the standard Steward bullet: stop list defined by passing it through the same stemmer, 'without' and other function words added, threshold of one shared stem for parts with three or fewer stems. The three standard Steward bullets are hand-traced in tests against ordinary criteria. (3) Minor, quoted complaints: an affirmative 'is a follow-up' pattern does not exempt a part when the sentence has a reporting cue (said, claimed, wrong, the reading, earlier, rejected). (4) Nit: the test comment states the sza7 request text is rebuilt from the brief, because records/ is absent. Its candidate changed nothing, so no work is kept.

Rules are a small deterministic spec. The false-refusal count is measured by a test over the Steward-bullet requests and existing reading-test fixtures in reading.rs, and that count is written in the CHANGELOG entry.
Job 20261029-110953-bw7k and job 20261029-084645-sza7 code stays as landed or dropped, as the earlier scope says; this job only touches the three listed files.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`: a test calls check_reading_acceptance on a scoped_reading whose out_of_scope defers 'Part (3)' to a follow-up, with the numbered-parts request of job 20261029-084645-sza7 (rebuilt from the brief, and the test comment says so). It is refused with an error naming part (3), and the test fails on the code before the change.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`: tests show `N.`, `N)` and lettered requests with no Acceptance heading are refused when item 3 is deferred or has no criterion, the same as `(N)`; a reading that covers every part with a criterion is accepted.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`: a reading with ordinary criteria for the three standard Steward bullets ('A test fails without the change and passes with it...', 'fmt, clippy and test pass', root cause named) is accepted. A request with no numbered parts is unaffected, and a request that itself says a part is a follow-up still accepts a reading deferring it.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`: a request that quotes a complaint ('the earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong') still refuses a reading that defers part (3).

Grep crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs: check_request_coverage exists, check_reading_acceptance calls it, and its doc comment names the root cause (no comparison of the request's named parts with the reading) and cites jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k.

This change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 5% of newly refused readings. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` to check that the existing reading tests and replay tests still pass.

Run `cargo test -p athena-context`: READING_RULES in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs gains one line about the coverage check and the rule-section size test (under 2400 bytes) passes, with the measured byte count stated in the CHANGELOG or test.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`: all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that names the root cause and the new coverage check, and the measured false-refusal count.

out_of_scope: Changing athena.toml, check_timeout_s or its schema; the timeout work landed in job 20261029-110953-bw7k and job 20261029-084645-sza7 stays rejected.
Job 20261029-110953-bw7k files (crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, status_durations.rs test, checks.rs, disk.rs, run/mod.rs, status.rs) stay as landed; its minor findings are not touched.
Job 20261029-084645-sza7 files (athena.toml, checks.rs, disk.rs, run/mod.rs, CHANGELOG.md) are dropped; that candidate was rejected.
Job 20261029-111202-2bpc left no candidate changes, so nothing from it is kept.
Editing reader or verifier prompt files, because the reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom.
departures: Higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: the same rule failed planning at round 3 before, and it is a hard-gate change with a tight rule-section byte cap.
urgent_reason: Cuts failed planning rounds and repeated rejected attempts: the earlier job stopped at round 3 of 3 on specification gaps in the same rule.
hard_reason: Adds a refusal rule to check_reading_acceptance, the gate every reading passes, so a mistake wrongly refuses readings.
